subject: Re: Dedicated capacity perf validation - SLOs & GPU sizing

Subject: Dedicated capacity perf validation - Acme: latency & sizing follow-up

Hi James / Acme SRE team,

Thanks again for the call earlier - good discussion. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on performance targets and what Redwood will validate on Dedicated:

Summary of SLOs you stated on the call:
- P95 latency target: <= 200 ms for 512-token responses when streaming is enabled (important for UX)
- Sustained concurrency: 40 concurrent active requests (peak spikes to ~60 for short periods)
- Min sustained throughput: ~20k tokens/sec across the pool during business hours
- Streaming required (chunked / server-sent events) for token-level UX

What Redwood will validate in the Dedicated proof-of-concept:
1) Baseline perf for your model/weights on H100 vs A100 using your representative dataset (attached perf-results-20260802.csv).
2) Sizing to meet P95 latency <=200ms at 40 concurrent requests, and tests covering 60-concurrency spikes.
3) Streaming verification (latency per first token, average chunk latencies) and fallback behavior when capacity constrained.
4) Recommended reserved throughput (tokens/sec) and number of GPUs for the target SLO + expected cost envelope.

Action items (proposed):
- Acme: share a 2-3 GB representative test bucket or Drive folder (we discussed a sanitized sample) - Marissa, Rafael, please confirm when available.
- Redwood (Aditya + Rafael): run H100/A100 comparatives and return sizing recs + a small SLA draft by EOD Monday.
- Set up a 60-minute canary run with synthetic and real traffic next week (TBD).

Attachments: perf-results-20260802.csv (initial microbenchmarks run on public finetuned-13B variant)

Thanks - I'll sync with Aditya and Rafael and we'll follow up with concrete numbers.

Best,

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity perf validation - initial sizing notes

Thanks Marissa - quick technical follow-up based on the perf CSV and the targets above. I ran the microbenchmarks this afternoon and annotated the attached CSV, but high-level notes below:

Model / HW perf (rough median numbers from our 13B fp16 runs):
- H100 (fp16, tuned kernels): ~2.5k tokens/sec per GPU (batch-aware, batch sizes 4-8, seq=512).
- A100 (fp16): ~1.6k tokens/sec per GPU under similar batching.
- L4 / L40S class: ~800-1k tokens/sec per GPU (more cost-efficient for lower SLOs).

Implications for your SLOs:
- To hit 20k tokens/sec sustained you'd need roughly 8 H100s (20k/2.5k = 8) or ~13 A100s.
- For p95 <= 200ms at 512 tokens with 40 concurrent, streaming adds a bit of overhead for first-byte latency. To keep p95 under 200ms we should target a headroom of ~30-40% above baseline capacity to cover queuing and KV cache cold-starts.
- My conservative recommendation: reserve 6 H100s with optimized batching + KV cache enabled for your workload, then run a canary to validate p95. If you see frequent spikes to 60 concurrency, we should plan autoscaling bursts or an additional 2 GPUs reserved.

Tuning notes:
- Use continuous batching and small max-batch-time (5-10 ms) to balance latency and throughput.
- Enable prefix KV cache for common contexts to reduce per-request compute.
- Quantization to int8 or 4-bit can further improve throughput; we should bench accuracy/regression on your eval set before recommending.

I'll kick off a comparative run (H100 vs A100) against the sample set if you grant access to the dataset. Rafael and I will produce a short sizing table + estimated monthly cost for the recommended reserve.

- Aditya
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa / Aditya - this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Budget sensitivity: we have tighter budget for Q3; if H100s are materially more expensive, can A100s be an acceptable tradeoff if we add an extra GPU for headroom?
- Spikes: we do see short bursts to ~60 concurrency during promos. Can we rely on autoscaling/burst capacity for those spikes, or do you recommend reserving headroom?
- Streaming fallback: if H100 pool is constrained, can streaming degrade gracefully to an A100 pool while preserving token-level streaming?

We'll share the sanitized sample dataset to the Drive link by EOD today. Also open to the canary next week - aiming for Aug 10-11.

-James

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity perf validation - proposed MAP & canary plan

Hi all - following up with a short mutual action plan and proposed canary:

Proposed MAP:
1) Acme uploads sanitized sample to https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeTestDataset (you mentioned this on the call).
2) Redwood runs H100 vs A100 comparatives using your sample (3x 30-minute runs across representative payloads). We will produce:
   - Sizing table (GPUs required, reserved throughput tokens/sec)
   - p95/p99 latency distribution, first-byte streaming latency, and cost estimate
   - Recommendations for autoscale/burst config to cover 60-concurrency spikes
3) Canary run: 4-hour window with production-like traffic (mixed synthetic + rewound traffic); Redwood will provide a canary dashboard and logs.
4) SLA draft and redlines (attached SLA-draft-Acme-Redwood-20260803.pdf).

Timeline: start comparatives Aug 4 (once sample is available); deliver initial sizing + cost by Aug 6; schedule canary Aug 10-11.

Notes on streaming fallback: Redwood runtime supports routing by policy - we can route to an A100 fallback pool preserving streaming behavior, but first-byte latency will be higher and p95 may slip depending on load. We'll include degradation matrices in the sizing doc.

Attachments: SLA-draft-Acme-Redwood-20260803.pdf

Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
